declarations.parity_review: Reviewed reuses an existing about:blank bootstrap page. Original body, setup, imports, lifecycle and every assertion operand match the bounded AST audit. The four page-selection tests retain each resolved reference identity check and the mock call-count assertion. The reviewed objects contain functions; the raw identity guard excludes custom serialization and unsupported descriptors. Real Vitest and Rust counterexamples distinguish matching references from equal-shaped different references. Every observation and an opposing counterexample agree between real Vitest and Rust. Bindings, per-site counts and source hashes: .jait/artifacts/parity-exceptions/source-checkpoint/.jait/artifacts/parity-identity-followup/combined-selected.json. Full translated, internal, managed, formatting and Clippy validation passed on the unchanged exception checkpoint. Candidate originals, peers, comparator and transport hashes also match the live checkout. The initial full report exposed a queue timing failure (expected 409, actual 200); that report and three isolated passing unmodified Vitest runs are retained in .jait/artifacts/parity-exceptions/queue-timing-observation.json. No queue assertion or application behavior was changed, and the subsequent complete full run passed. This establishes preservation of the exercised reference-test domains, not native runtime parity or absence of reference-test flakes.
